title: Training for the Jobs Between Departments
transcript:
A regional hospital has introduced a training programme for staff whose work moves between departments. The participants are not doctors or nurses. They transport equipment, prepare rooms and deliver supplies. Their tasks can appear routine, but a missed message between teams may cause delays that spread through the building.

The programme began after managers reviewed a series of postponed appointments. In several cases, equipment had been delivered to the correct department but left in a storage area without anyone being told. The delivery team considered its task complete, while the receiving team believed the equipment had not arrived. Neither group had a reliable record of the handover.

Rather than adding another general lecture about communication, trainers asked mixed groups of employees to reconstruct a typical delivery from beginning to end. Each group marked the points at which responsibility changed. This exercise revealed that different departments used the same word, ready, to mean different things. In one unit it meant that equipment had arrived; in another it meant that the equipment had been checked and could be used.

The hospital introduced a short handover record with separate entries for arrival and inspection. Staff practised using it during ordinary shifts, and supervisors collected examples of confusing situations. The first review found fewer calls asking whether a delivery had been made, although it was too early to measure any effect on overall waiting times.

One supervisor says the programme has changed which employees are included in discussions about service quality. People who connect departments often see problems that remain invisible within a single team. The hospital plans to keep those workers involved as the record is revised, rather than treating their training as a completed one-off event.

questions.prompt: Who is the hospital’s new training programme mainly intended for?
options: Employees who move equipment and supplies between departments.
questions.answer: Employees who move equipment and supplies between departments.
questions.explanation: 培训对象是运送设备、准备房间和配送物资等跨部门支持人员。

questions.prompt: What problem contributed to the delayed appointments?
options: Equipment arrived but its handover was not reliably communicated.
All deliveries were sent to the wrong hospital.
The receiving teams refused to inspect any equipment.
Patients were asked to transport their own supplies.
questions.answer: Equipment arrived but its handover was not reliably communicated.
questions.explanation: 物品虽送达正确部门，但未通知接收方，也无可靠交接记录。

questions.prompt: What did the mixed-group exercise reveal about the word ready?
options: It was never used by the delivery staff.
It had different practical meanings in different departments.
It referred only to the departure of a transport vehicle.
It had already been removed from all hospital records.
questions.answer: It had different practical meanings in different departments.
questions.explanation: 不同部门把 ready 理解为已到货或已检查可使用，含义并不相同。

questions.prompt: What was established by the first review?
options: The programme had eliminated all appointment delays.
Overall waiting times had fallen by a known amount.
The new record no longer needed revision.
There were fewer calls asking whether equipment had arrived.
questions.answer: There were fewer calls asking whether equipment had arrived.
questions.explanation: 初步观察发现询问送达情况的电话减少，但总体等待时间影响尚未测定。
